## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Veḷukajātaka* (Ja 43) is a short narrative belonging to the *Jātaka* collection of the Pali Canon [SuttaCentral; Anandajoti 2010]. The narrative is framed at Jetavana, where the Buddha addresses a headstrong or obstinate monk (*dubbacabhikkhu*) [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1877]. Revealing that the monk possessed this same stubborn disposition in a previous existence, the Buddha recounts a story of the past in which an ascetic refused to heed the warnings of the Bodhisatta, the leader of the ascetic community [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1877]. Despite the Bodhisatta's advice, the ascetic took in and nurtured a young venomous snake (*āsīvisapotaka*), which eventually bit and killed him [UNDV Conference 2009; Rahula 1978]. In modern ethical and ecological analyses of the *Jātaka*s, this narrative has been discussed as an example of misplaced compassion, showing that nurturing inherently destructive things can lead to disaster [UNDV Conference 2009].

The central canonical verse encapsulates the moral warning that whoever disregards the guidance of well-wishing friends meets destruction just like "Veḷuka's father" (*Veḷukapitā*) [Appleton 2010; Fausböll 1877]. In the story's conclusion (*samodhāna*), the headstrong monk is identified as Veḷukapitā, the Buddha's assembly as the former ascetic community, and the Bodhisatta as the group's leader [Fausböll 1877].

No early cross-language parallels in Chinese, Tibetan, or Sanskrit are listed by SuttaCentral or identified by DharmaNexus with a score of 10 or above [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus registers internal Pali text reuse across five segments (totaling 392 characters) with the prose commentary of the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (longest match §0.4–1.4 matching §1617_11–1620 at 0.93 similarity), representing the shared canonical verse and its explanatory apparatus [DharmaNexus].
